source: EZ Draft Build Specification, Phases and tickets tab, doc revision 634, exported Oct 11, 2026

phases.name: Setup
phases.goal_and_gate:
Goal: a deployed, empty, multi-tenant app with sign-in and the Studio shell components, ready for features.
**Build gate:** the app deploys to a preview URL; in the browser test a signed-in tenant 1 user sees the empty editor shell at desktop and iPad landscape sizes; a test user of a second tenant reads zero tenant 1 rows; the performance check (EZD-017) runs in CI and passes on the empty shell. **Field check (Josh):** open ezdraft.ezcontractorbinder.com on the desktop and the iPad.

phases.name: Foundation
phases.goal_and_gate:
Goal: users, permissions, projects, customers, versions, the edit lock, notifications and the event log work end to end before any drawing tool exists.
**Build gate:** against the EZ Binder stub (EZD-019), create a project from a stub job; pass the Edit lock acceptance test with two browser sessions (amber banner with holder and time; Request edit prompts the holder; no answer for the release time saves and releases; banner turns green); the Projects page shows its first cards within budget with 200 seeded projects. **Field check (Josh):** repeat the EZ Binder steps against the real EZ Binder once its side of the contract is built.

phases.name: Geometry core + plan editor
phases.goal_and_gate:
Goal: draw and edit existing conditions and a new design in plan with typed lengths, on one parametric model.
**Build gate:** the Measurement entry, Room closure, Wall move and Selection acceptance tests pass as automated tests, and on the benchmark project pan, zoom and a wall drag stay inside the frame budget. **Field check (Josh):** draw an existing kitchen from tape measurements faster than by hand.

phases.name: Imports
phases.goal_and_gate:
Goal: bring a Polycam scan, a PDF or a DXF into the model through Import review, with typed and laser values overriding the scan.
**Build gate:** the Import acceptance test passes on the fixture Polycam scan, vector PDF and DXF (low-confidence items highlighted; nothing enters the model before accept; a typed override lists its conflicts). **Field check (Josh):** import a real Polycam scan from a current job and fix it.

phases.name: Cabinets + countertops
phases.goal_and_gate:
Goal: build cabinet runs from real boxes with elevations and a schedule, then countertops with overhangs, seams, cutouts and edge profiles.
**Build gate:** the Cabinets and Countertops acceptance tests pass (auto-fill of a 117 1/2" wall gives 3" boxes plus filler with total vs wall; trace creates pieces; a 12" seating side shows the brackets notice; exposed LF matches the fixture's hand count). **Field check (Josh):** reproduce a past kitchen's cabinet order.

phases.name: Ceilings / RCP
phases.goal_and_gate:
Goal: edit each room's ceiling and the objects on it, and produce the reflected ceiling plan data for sheet A6.0.
**Build gate:** a fixture room with a sloped ceiling, beams, cans and an ACT area is built by the browser test, and the first half of the RCP acceptance test passes (ACT borders never below half a tile). The second half (lights on E1.0 with the same circuit) closes in EZD-708. **Field check (Josh):** draw the RCP for a real room.

phases.name: Electrical + code check
phases.goal_and_gate:
Goal: place devices, circuit them, run the NEC 220 residential load calc and panel schedule, and run code checks (2023 NEC and Florida Building Code rule sets) on demand from any editor tab.
**Build gate:** the Electrical acceptance test passes: the load calc reproduces the worked example in Calculations, and on the fixture house Check lists a missing GFCI, a toilet drawn closer than 15" to a side wall and a bedroom with no emergency escape opening, each with its code section, and shows the water heater checklist reminders; a CI test confirms every rule in the catalog file is registered. **Field check (Josh):** compare the load calc for a real job with your own.

phases.name: Sheets, issue, submittal profiles, revisions, property appraiser import
phases.goal_and_gate:
Goal: auto-build the sheet set, pass the issue gates, and issue Rev 0 and numbered revisions as PDFs that follow each department's submittal profile.
**Build gate:** the Sheets, Revisions and RCP acceptance tests pass (key shows only used symbols; issue blocked by an orphan flag; check dimension measures true in the exported PDF; an edit after Rev 0 sent to the client becomes Rev 1 with clouds on exactly the changed objects; RCP lights appear on E1.0 with the same circuit), and the PDFs exported under each seeded department profile pass automated checks for page size, file split, file names, bookmarks and size limit. **Field check (Josh):** a set accepted by a building department.

phases.name: Detail editor
phases.goal_and_gate:
Goal: draw custom 2D details with parts, hatches, line roles, keynotes and steps, place them on sheets, and extrude closed profiles to 3D.
**Build gate:** the browser test draws the floating-shelf detail, places it on A5.0 after print preview with its “3 / A5.0” callout, and extrudes its profile. **Field check (Josh):** draw a detail from a current job.

phases.name: Reference DXF + supplier imports + rendering markup
phases.goal_and_gate:
Goal: show architect and supplier DXFs at full fidelity under the model, mark them up, compare versions, and tie supplier renderings and order reports to the plan's cabinet boxes.
**Build gate:** each fixture DXF draws every entity the parser reports (entity counts per layer match); pan and zoom over the benchmark DXF stay inside the frame budget; every mismatch between the fixture order report and the plan can be resolved. **Field check (Josh):** open 2–3 real architect DXFs on the iPad, and resolve a real supplier order report against the plan when a sample is available.

phases.name: 3D + design options
phases.goal_and_gate:
Goal: show the live 3D model with orbit, walk, look up, section and saved views, and build design options A/B/C with internal costs.
**Build gate:** the benchmark kitchen opens in 3D within budget; saved views, section and walk pass their browser tests; options A/B/C for a ceiling show their internal cost deltas; the exported GLB passes glTF validation and loads in a model-viewer test page. **Field check (Josh):** a real kitchen opens in 3D on the iPad without memory errors, and the GLB displays in EZ Binder's model viewer.

phases.name: Render pipeline + allowance + local GPU worker
phases.goal_and_gate:
Goal: run angle-first AI renders in three tiers, review and approve them in two steps, and track spend in dollars against a self-refilling allowance, using the local GPU worker first.
**Build gate:** the Render acceptance test passes with the stub provider (Generate disabled until an angle is chosen; an unapproved render is never client-ready), and a job goes to the worker protocol when a worker heartbeat is present and to the cloud adapter when it is not. **Field check (Josh):** a photoreal render of a real job runs on the local worker, then on the cloud API with the worker off.

phases.name: Client link
phases.goal_and_gate:
Goal: the homeowner views renders and plans on a phone, comments, chooses options and edges, verifies, signs and approves, and gets a selections PDF.
**Build gate:** the Client acceptance test passes in a phone-size browser test (signature logs name, date and IP; approval locks the version; the link expires at 30 days and renews), and the client page meets its download-size budget with no editor or 3D code. **Field check (Josh):** a real client approves selections from a phone.

phases.name: Change orders + EZ Binder webhooks and inbound API
phases.goal_and_gate:
Goal: send signed, retried events to EZ Binder, answer its inbound calls, and turn a revision into a change order draft that reaches EZ Binder only on Send.
**Build gate:** against the EZ Binder stub, a revision produces a CO that is sent, and the stub marking it approved locks the matching revision; the Webhooks acceptance test passes (each outbound event is signed, retried on failure, and logged). **Field check (Josh):** a client signs a real CO in EZ Binder.

phases.name: Field pack + offline + field measurements review
phases.goal_and_gate:
Goal: crews use a room-by-room phone field pack offline, and the office approves field measurements before they change the model; the lock holder can edit offline without loss.
**Build gate:** the Offline and Field acceptance tests pass in browser tests with the network switched off and on (the holder edits offline and reconnects with every queued change in a new version; a field measurement changes the model only after approval; a conflict notifies the office), and the field pack meets its download-size budget. **Field check (Josh):** a crew uses the field pack on a live job for a week.

phases.name: Translations
phases.goal_and_gate:
Goal: AI-drafted Spanish for notes, keynotes and field tasks, reviewed in one queue and reused across jobs, with Spanish users always seeing Spanish.
**Build gate:** signed in as a Spanish-language user, the fixture field pack shows no English task or note text, and the Translations acceptance test passes (editing an approved phrase updates every use; the hold setting holds only set issue). **Field check (Josh):** a Spanish-speaking crew member reads the whole field pack.

phases.name: Catalog + takeoff
phases.goal_and_gate:
Goal: a full product catalog filled by link, pasted text or screenshot with confirmed AI fields and project price snapshots, and takeoff quantities by room and trade with waste factors.
**Build gate:** products are added from recorded link, pasted-text and screenshot fixtures with every field confirmed; the takeoff CSV for the fixture kitchen matches its hand count; the Permissions acceptance test passes (unticking See company costs removes every company cost, and unticking See sell prices every sell price, markup and total, from that user's views and exports). **Field check (Josh):** add ten real products and check a takeoff against a real kitchen.

phases.name: Hardening
phases.goal_and_gate:
Goal: confirm the performance targets on Josh's iPad (they are enforced from Phase 0), prove backups restore, close security gaps, and publish the terms.
**Build gate:** every budget in Non-functional requirements (Performance) holds on the benchmark project in CI, the restore script passes, the automated security suite (EZD-1705) passes, and the terms page renders. **Field check (Josh):** pan and zoom hold 60 fps on the desktop and 30 fps on the iPad with real architect DXFs, and a real project opens within budget; a full-house model runs in iPad Safari without a crash; monthly and per-render costs are recorded against the estimate; on the first job in each place the unverified department items are confirmed and the profiles updated; every code rule is marked verified in Settings 15g.

tickets.title: Repo and tooling
tickets.scope: Next.js + React + TypeScript app; lint, format, type check, unit test runner; empty geometry-core package with no UI code. Uses the tools named in the conventions file (pnpm workspace, Vitest).
tickets.done_when: App builds; a sample unit test in the geometry package passes.

tickets.title: CI
tickets.scope: Pipeline runs lint, type check and tests on every push; preview deploy per branch.
tickets.done_when: CI runs lint, type check and tests on every push; a commit with a failing test makes the CI run fail. Preview deploys are checked in EZD-003.

tickets.scope: Vercel project; DNS record for ezdraft.ezcontractorbinder.com pointing to Vercel; HTTPS.
tickets.done_when: The app loads at the subdomain over HTTPS.

tickets.title: Supabase project
tickets.scope: Supabase Pro with Postgres, Auth, Storage, Realtime; dev and prod; env config; migrations run in CI. Agent test runs use a local Supabase; the cloud projects and keys come from Josh (Needs from Josh).
tickets.done_when: Migrations apply to the local Supabase in CI and the app reads a health row; applying to the cloud dev project waits for Josh's keys.

tickets.title: Tenant, user, membership tables
tickets.scope: tenant (name, logo, license_no, contact, title_block, code_edition, defaults json); user (name, email required, language, ipad_input_mode); membership (status invited / active / deactivated, invited_at, last_active_at, scope all or listed projects; role_id is added by EZD-101); membership_project (the listed projects of a scoped user). project (fields per Data model, plus archived_at, thumbnail_path, open_items_count). user also carries role_preset.
tickets.done_when: Seed creates Worth Properties as tenant 1 with Josh as owner.

tickets.title: Row-level security
tickets.scope: RLS policy on every table by tenant_id; helper for users scoped to listed projects; policy test harness. The tenant id is read from the session claim once per query (no membership join per row); every table gets an index on tenant_id and, where present, project_id. A token hook sets the active tenant claim; deactivating a user or changing their project scope ends their sessions; a CI test fails when a table has no policy or lacks its tenant and project indexes.
tickets.done_when: Tenant B user gets zero rows from tenant A; a scoped user sees only listed projects. A deactivated user's next request is refused.

tickets.title: Magic-link sign-in
tickets.scope: Supabase Auth email magic link, session, sign-out; no passwords. The email carries the link and a 6-digit code that can be typed into the installed app (a link opened from email does not sign in an installed iPad or iPhone app); field devices keep a long-lived session.
tickets.done_when: In a browser test the link is read from the local Supabase mail catcher; the user signs in with it and signs out. Typing the 6-digit code signs in without opening the link.
tickets.spec_ref: Users and role presets; Non-functional · Security

tickets.title: Email provider
tickets.scope: Transactional email setup on the app domain; send helper that also returns the link so the UI can show Copy link. A stub transport, chosen by env, records messages for tests.
tickets.done_when: With the stub transport, the helper records one message and returns the same link URL that is in the message body. Live delivery is a field check.

tickets.title: Background job queue
tickets.scope: job table in Postgres (kind, payload, status, progress, attempts, error, run_after) for imports, exports, renders and AI reads; workers run as Vercel Functions started on enqueue and by a once-a-minute sweep; a job is split so one run fits the function time limit; retry with backoff; progress pushed on the project Realtime channel (EZD-018), no polling. Jobs are claimed with a row lock and a lease that expires; handlers are safe to run twice; job inputs and outputs are Storage paths, never request bodies.
tickets.done_when: A test job runs, reports progress and result, and the UI stays usable; two workers started at once run the job once; a job whose run dies is picked up again after its lease expires.

tickets.title: Fixtures

tickets.title: Performance budgets and benchmark
tickets.scope: CI check that counts React commits during a scripted pan, draw calls per frame, buffers rebuilt per edit, long tasks, rows written per save and compressed JavaScript size per entry point, and records frame times, project open time, tab switch time and autosave time as a trend, against the budgets in Non-functional requirements (Performance); results written to a file on every run. The benchmark project comes from EZD-236. Later tickets add their own measurements to this check.
tickets.done_when: The check fails when an extra React commit during a pan or an oversize bundle is introduced, and passes on the empty shell.

tickets.title: Realtime channels
tickets.scope: One helper over Supabase Realtime: a channel per open project (lock state, presence, job progress, review count) and a channel per user (notifications); on reconnect, resubscribe and refetch once; no polling loops anywhere in the app. Subscribing to a project channel is authorized against the user's project scope.
tickets.done_when: Two browser sessions see each other's presence and a test broadcast event with no page refresh and no timer-driven request. A scoped user cannot subscribe to a project outside their list.

tickets.title: EZ Binder contract and stub
tickets.scope: Written contract (an OpenAPI file in the repo, copied to the vault) for every call between the apps: job search and read, customer list and upsert, user list, shared sign-on token and return-to-job URL, webhook receiver, Mark change order approved; a stub EZ Binder server that implements it for tests, with seeded jobs and customers; the stub base URL is an env value. The contract also defines the sign-on exchange (EZ Binder asks for a single-use 60-second code bound to a user and a project; EZ Draft swaps it on the server for a session) and that the webhook address, signing secret and inbound key are entered at Connect (EZD-114).
tickets.done_when: Contract tests pass against the stub, and the contract lists request and response fields for every call.
tickets.spec_ref: Hooks, events and integrations; Relationship to EZ Binder

tickets.title: Entry points and lazy chunks
tickets.scope: Separate entry points for Projects and Settings, the editor, the phone field pack and the client link; a lazy-module pattern for heavy libraries (Three.js 3D scene, three-bvh-csg, path tracer, pdf.js, DXF parser and writer, GLB and USDZ exporters) and for the Detail editor, Sheets and the catalog drawer; a lint rule that refuses static imports of those libraries outside their lazy modules; bundle report in CI.
tickets.done_when: A static Three.js import added to the Projects page fails CI; the client link and field pack bundles contain no editor or 3D code.

tickets.title: AI client and stubs
tickets.scope: Server helper for Claude text and image calls, always run through the job queue; API key from env; stub providers with recorded responses for Claude and the image models (the email stub is in EZD-008), used by every test; a test that reaches a live provider fails the suite.
tickets.done_when: A queued test job returns the stub response; with no key set a live job fails with “AI key not set”.

tickets.title: Event registry
tickets.scope: Typed registry of every event name in Hooks, events and integrations, plus an emit() helper; every later ticket emits through it. The event log write is added by EZD-109 and webhook delivery by EZD-1301.
tickets.done_when: A unit test fails when code emits a name that is not in the registry.

tickets.title: Architecture conventions
tickets.scope: docs/architecture.md and CLAUDE.md in the repo, copied to the vault: one named, version-pinned choice for every row of Stack · Named tools; the folder layout (app, packages/geometry, worker, spikes); the server-only data access pattern and the can() helper; migration naming; the error handling and logging pattern; Storage bucket and path layout; test naming; how a ticket adds a dependency (an entry in the file in the same commit); the handoff file path and format. A lint rule or CI check for every rule a machine can check. Where the spec names no library, the builder picks one and records it here, and later tickets reuse it.
tickets.done_when: Both files exist with a choice for every Named tools row; CI fails when package.json holds a dependency the file does not list.

tickets.title: Environments and release
tickets.scope: Local, dev and production environments; preview deploys use the dev database; production is updated only by a promote script run on a tagged build, which first takes a database dump; a CI check that refuses a migration which drops or renames something the previous tag still reads; rollback steps in the runbook.
tickets.done_when: CI fails a fixture migration that drops a column the previous tag reads; the promote script refuses an untagged build.

tickets.title: Error reporting
tickets.scope: Sentry in the browser, the functions and the render worker, with a stub transport in tests; an email to the owner on a new error, a failed job or a failed webhook.
tickets.done_when: A thrown test error reaches the stub transport and queues one owner email; a second identical error queues none.

tickets.title: Off-site backups and restore script
tickets.scope: A nightly job copies new Storage objects to a bucket at a second provider (object versioning on) and a weekly job writes a database dump there; a restore script loads a dump and the copied files into a scratch local Supabase and checks that a deleted test project is back; the restore runbook goes in the vault; deletes of sent-package files are soft deletes.
tickets.done_when: The restore script passes in CI against the local Supabase and a stub bucket. Field check: Josh runs the drill on the cloud project before the first real job is entered.

tickets.done_when: Lint fails on a literal string in a phone-screen component; a test page renders in Spanish for a Spanish user.

tickets.title: Model store, outbox and editor route
tickets.scope: In-memory patch store (Zustand): every edit is a patch applied locally at once, the same patches drive undo, and the store reports which object ids changed so views and derived values update only for those; one IndexedDB outbox that every write goes into, drained by autosave 2 seconds after the last edit with one save in flight, each change carrying its base updated_seq and the lock_epoch (Architecture rule 9); the open working copy mirrored in IndexedDB; the editor route, which loads a project in one query; header save state (Saving…, Saved just now, Saved N min ago); save error banner with Retry, edits kept.
tickets.done_when: 50 edits in one minute write only the changed model_object rows and no model_version row; with the network off the edits stay in the outbox and drain on reconnect; a failed save shows the banner and loses nothing.

tickets.title: Reference conversion job

Entity types the parser cannot read are counted per type and stored with the reference. The ticket commits a generator for a fixture architect DXF (layers, blocks, hatches, text, dims, two paper-space layouts) and a revised copy (one wall moved, one entity added, one removed, one dim value changed) with expected-count JSON, and adds the 150,000-entity DXF to the benchmark project.
tickets.done_when: For the fixture DXF the entity count per layer in the buffers equals the parser's count, and an entity type the parser does not support appears in the not-read count.

tickets.done_when: Opening a project with the fixture reference keeps the Plan interactive while layers load (no main-thread task over 50 ms in the test trace); the reference chunk is not requested on a project with no reference; pan and zoom over the benchmark DXF stay inside the performance check. Field check: a real architect DXF matches its source, layer for layer.
